title: Chapter 1 Mrs. Gorf Mrs. Gorf had a long tongue and pointed ears. She was the meanest teacher in Wayside School. She taught the class on the thirtieth story.
location: Sala de aula da Escola Wayside — Trigésimo Andar

beats.action_pt: Mrs. Gorf fica ereta atrás da mesa, orelhas pontiagudas trêmulas enquanto avisa à classe. Seus olhos estreitam com desdém, lábios se curvando em um sorriso cruel. A iluminação de tungstênio cria sombras profundas sob seu queixo, destacando a textura áspera de seu vestido marrom e o brilho úmido de sua língua prestes a sair.
beats.narration: "If you children are bad," she warned, "or if you answer a problem wrong, I’ll wiggle my ears, stick out my tongue, and turn you into apples!" Mrs. Gorf didn’t like children, but she loved apples.

beats.action_pt: A classe inteira fica paralisada, três maçãs vermelhas brilhando na mesa onde Joe, John e Todd estavam. Stephen soluça silenciosamente, ombros tremendo, mãos apertando as coias até ficar branco. Mrs. Gorf atravessa o sala com passos deliberados, sombra alongando-se atrás dela enquanto se aproxima do menino chorando.
beats.narration:
Then she turned John into an apple for letting Joe cheat.

“Hey, that isn’t fair,” said Todd. “John was only trying to help a friend.” Mrs. Gorf wiggled her ears—first her right one, then her left—stuck out her tongue, and turned Todd into an apple. “Does anybody else have an opinion?” she asked.

Nobody said a word.

Mrs. Gorf laughed and placed the three apples on her desk.

Stephen started to cry. He couldn’t help it. He was scared.

“I do not allow crying in the classroom,” said Mrs. Gorf.

beats.action_pt: Louis enters from left frame, yard teacher's whistle around neck, casual stride stopping dead as he sees the apple on desk, children frozen in silence behind him, his eyebrows rising in confusion then dawning realization as he sniffs the air, dust motes dancing in afternoon light streaming through high windows.
beats.narration:
The children didn’t know what to do. They didn’t have a teacher. Even though Mrs. Gorf was mean, they didn’t think it was right to leave her as an apple. But none of them knew how to wiggle their ears.

Louis, the yard teacher, walked in. “Where’s Mrs. Gorf?” he asked.

Nobody said a word.

“Boy, am I hungry,” said Louis. “I don’t think Mrs. Gorf would mind if I ate this apple.
